warning: In the page model the batch (64) and d_model (64) are the same number. To know which is which, look at the position: the batch is always the first axis.

steps.title: Token ids
steps.text: The digits and the words become ids. The decoder input starts with <bos>.

steps.title: Look up the embeddings
steps.text: Each id picks one row of the embedding table: 6 numbers per digit.

steps.title: Scale by √d_model
steps.text: Multiply by √6 ≈ 2.45. The table started with numbers of size about 1/√6, so the scaled rows are about as long as the position rows in the next step. Here the token rows are 3.2 and 2.3 long, and each position row 1.7. Neither one is much bigger than the other.

steps.title: Add the positions
steps.text: Add row 0 of the position table to the first digit and row 1 to the second.

steps.title: Encoder self-attention
steps.text: Every digit scores every digit (Q and K both from the digits). No causal mask: the encoder may read the whole number. Here no PAD needs blocking.

tensors.name: scores = Q Kᵀ / √d_k
tensors.note: The page model has 4 heads, so its scores have a head axis.

steps.title: Add & norm, then the FFN
steps.text: Add x to the attention output, then LayerNorm 1 normalizes the sum. Then the FFN widens each digit to d_ff = 12 numbers, applies ReLU, and narrows it back to 6. Add and normalize again (LayerNorm 2). The result is the memory: one vector per digit, computed once.

steps.title: Decoder input
steps.text: The words go through the same three steps: look up, scale by √d_model, add positions.

steps.title: Masked self-attention
steps.text: Words score earlier words only. The causal mask is 3 × 3 because both Q and K come from the decoder input, which has 3 tokens. Blocked scores become −∞, and their weights 0.

steps.title: Cross-attention
steps.text: Q comes from the 3 words, K and V from the 2 digits in memory. So the scores are 3 × 2: for each word, how much weight it gives each digit. No causal mask: the whole number is known.

steps.title: Add & norm, FFN
steps.text: The same residual, LayerNorm and FFN as in the encoder. This is the decoder output.

steps.title: Output layer: logits
steps.text: One row of 32 scores per position. When the model writes, only the last row counts: its top word is the next word. When it trains, every row is compared with tgt_out.
